findings: Fourteen frames arrive; thirteen have a sole-indirect topology receipt, and one precedes sole-display confirmation. The complete desktop and Run dialog are visually verified; preceding frames 9 through 13 show no Run dialog. The first Run dialog arrives 268.836856 seconds after Win+R.

The input controller types notepad and presses Enter only after manual Run verification. The last received sole-display frame shows the partially updated Run input. Notepad appears only after the ordinary display is restored; that is not NPU display evidence.

One complete DWM capture records a 397x174 BGRA target, 413x213 BGRA source, six vertices and bilinear clamp sampler. The pixel shader samples RGB, replaces alpha with 1, then multiplies by a vertex color. Unchanged v221 CPU replay rejects this combination during linear executor construction; the rectangle executor deliberately limited alpha replacement to point filtering.

The stream records 565 successful requests and matching positive acknowledgements, including seventeen prewarm requests. One negative relay response matches the opaque-linear failure. Later device-lost DDI rejections are retained separately. Worker shutdown reports socket closed or timed out.
The observer stops on a DWM DDI rejection, removes both custom drivers, restores the ordinary display and clears the stream configuration. No physical driver or power setting is changed.

Compile metadata is associated in stream order; PID/sequence pairs repeat. A metadata event for the failed request has no successful result and is retained separately, verified against the negative relay receipt.

Successful triangle draws spend 68995.252 ms inside draw timers and 231656.748 ms outside them. Of 564 model operations, 534 hit the persistent cache. Outside-draw time includes model setup and graph construction, and is not solely compiler time. These totals do not establish a controlled comparison to v111.
Full desktop offload, usable interaction, physical scanout migration and Tahoma improvement remain unverified.
